body.para: Specifies the format that is used to display dates. This is the FoxPro version of the SET DATE command, which also accepts an expression.

SET DATE [TO] <cDateFormat>
SET DATE [TO] (<cExpression>)
SET DATE [TO] <function>(<Arguments>)
SET DATE [TO] &<cMacro>

<cDateFormat>One of the following keywords: AMERICAN, ANSI, BRITISH, DMY, FRENCH, GERMAN, ITALIAN, DUTCH, JAPAN, JAPANESE, TAIWAN, MDY, USA, YMD, SHORT, SYSTEM. SHORT uses the short date format of the operating system, like SYSTEM. The keyword LONG is not supported and generates an error.
(<cExpression>)An expression between parentheses, a function call or a macro (&) that returns a string with one of the keywords above, or a date picture such as "DD.MM.YYYY".

The command calls the function SetDateCountry() for the keywords and SetDateFormat() for the date pictures. An error is generated when the value is not a string or is not a known keyword or date picture.

SET DATE TO GERMAN
SET DATE TO ("DD/MM/YYYY")
SET DATE, SET DATE FORMAT, SET CENTURY
